newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Costello sees growth above four pct.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Costello sees growth above four pct.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday the economy could grow faster than four percent if inflation remained under control.
"I think if we can kill the savings problem and if we can beat inflation, we should be looking at an economy that grows at four percent plus," he told reporters.
The government has projected growth of 3.75 percent in fiscal 1997/98 (July-June).
But Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane said recently the economy could grow at least 4.5 percent a year over the next few years without triggering a blowout in inflation.
Latest official data shows the economy grew 2.4 percent in the year to March, 1997. But new data due on September 3 is expected to show stronger annual growth.
Costello said strong growth and a more flexible labour system were needed to combat unemployment.
Australia's unemployment rate rose to 8.7 percent in July from 8.5 percent a month earlier. It has remained stuck around 8.5 percent for the past two years.

The government has forecast the jobless rate to fall to 8.0 percent by the June quarter of 1998, and Costello and Treasury secretary Ted Evans have said it may even dip slightly below that level by mid-1998.
Costello said higher growth, higher national savings and labour reforms were the key to lower undemployment.
"With that you'll see an improvement in employment as we're expecting over the course of this year," he said.
"... the more flexibility you can get in practice in the labour market, the better you'll do in relation to employment.
"People have got to understand the better your wage and industrial relations system, the better an outcome you'll get in relation to employment."
